title: Tensor presentation of the kernel of restriction between nested ideals
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $J\subseteq I$ be ideal sheaf data [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and let $r_K:A_X\to(i_K)_*A_{Z_K}$ be additive restriction [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction]. Let $T_X$ be the sheafified lifted tensor-sections functor [lem-sc-etale-tensor-sections-right-exact], and $a:J.\mathrm{toModules}\to I.\mathrm{toModules}$ the specified inclusion. There exists an isomorphism $e:T_X(I)\cong\ker r_I$ for which $T_X(a)e$ is a kernel of $f:\ker r_I\to A_X\to(i_J)_*A_{Z_J}$. Explicitly $(T_X(a)e)f=0$ and the corresponding kernel fork is limiting. No module quotient, nilpotence, or square-zero assumption is made.

proof.text: Use the tensor ideal identifications for I and J and their compatibility with ideal inclusion.

Use the nested additive ideal kernel fork and its compatibility with the inclusions into the structure sheaf. Cancel the monomorphic kernel inclusion to identify the tensor map with eJ.hom followed by this fork inclusion.
The identified composite is zero. Transport the limiting fork along eJ using Mathlib IsKernel.isoKernel, and assemble the existential presentation.

theorem exists_etaleIdealKernelPresentation (X : Scheme.{u})
    (I J : X.IdealSheafData) (hJI : J ≤ I) :
    ∃ e : (Modules.etaleTensorSectionsFunctor X).obj I.toModules ≅
        kernel (etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar I.subschemeι),
      ∃ hzero : ((Modules.etaleTensorSectionsFunctor X).map
          (IdealSheafData.toModulesOfLE hJI) ≫ e.hom) ≫
          (kernel.ι (etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar I.subschemeι) ≫
            etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar J.subschemeι) = 0,
        Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι
          ((Modules.etaleTensorSectionsFunctor X).map
            (IdealSheafData.toModulesOfLE hJI) ≫ e.hom) hzero))
